title: How to Build a Retirement Plan if You Want to Travel Part-Time
description: Budgeting for the 'Snowbird' or 'Slow Travel' lifestyle.
content:
Many retirees don't want to move to Florida full-time; they want to keep a home base and travel for 3-6 months a year. This 'Part-Time Nomad' lifestyle offers the best of both worlds but is the most expensive way to retire because you are duplicating costs. You pay for an empty house in the US while paying for Airbnbs or hotels abroad. To make this work without running out of money, you need a 'Travel Sinking Fund' and a strategy to minimize home carrying costs while away.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Double Carry' Cost: You are paying utilities, taxes, and insurance on an empty house. Budget 1.5x your normal living expenses during travel months.
  • Rent It Out: The most effective hack is to rent your home while away (Airbnb/Furnished Finder). Income from 3 months of rental can often pay for 3 months of travel expenses.
  • The Travel Bucket: Create a separate savings account for travel. Fund it with 'lumpy' income (dividends/bonuses) rather than monthly withdrawals. When the bucket is empty, you go home.
  • Medical Logistics: Medicare doesn't cover you abroad. You need a Travel Medical policy ($200-$500/trip) or a global Expat Insurance plan.

Why It Matters (US Context)

If you rent your primary home for less than 15 days a year, the income is tax-free (Augusta Rule). If you rent it more, it is taxable, but you can deduct expenses. This tax code nuance can fund a 2-week luxury vacation annually tax-free.

The Travel Budget

Scenario: 3 Months in Europe annually.

Fixed Home Costs

Mortgage/Tax/Ins: $2,500/mo.
Utilities (min): $200/mo.
Cost while empty: $2,700/mo.

Travel Costs

Airbnb (Monthly Rate): $2,500/mo.
Flights: $1,500.
Food/Fun: $2,000/mo.
Total Trip Cost (3 mo): $15,000.

The Net Impact

Total Annual Spend: Base Budget + $15,000.
Portfolio Impact: You need an extra $375,000 in your nest egg (4% rule) to support this habit forever.

Cost Reduction Tactics

  1. Home Exchange: Swap homes with someone in London or Paris. Cost = $0. This is the only way to erase the 'Double Carry' cost entirely.
  2. Slow Travel: Staying in one city for 1 month gets you a 40-50% Airbnb discount compared to nightly rates. Stop moving every 3 days.
  3. Credit Card Points: Put all your home expenses on travel cards. The points earned from 'boring' bills can pay for your international flights.
  4. Turn Off Services: Suspend cable, internet (if possible), and trash service at home while away. Save $200/mo.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a house sitter?

Yes. Check your insurance policy. Some deny claims if the house is vacant for >30 days. You need someone to check pipes/mail.

Is an RV cheaper?

Not always. Gas + Campsites + Depreciation can equal the cost of Airbnbs. RVing is a lifestyle choice, not always a savings choice.

Can I just sell the house?

Yes. Going 'Full Nomad' eliminates the double carry. Invest the home equity ($500k) to generate $20k/year of extra travel income. This is the most efficient financial move.
